title: Toilet Flange Replacement and Toilet Installation (Compression Flange) Tutorial

locations.name: probable bathroom floor
locations.basis: Transcript references to a toilet, tile floor, and closet bend, implying a bathroom setting; no explicit shooting location is given.

summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing a wobbling toilet caused by an elevated, broken cast-iron closet flange and walks through replacing the flange with a compression flange, securing it to the floor, providing a wax-ring seal to the toilet, and finishing with bolt cap trimming and a wiggle test to verify stability. The speaker notes the flange’s height relative to the old floor, removes and replaces the brittle cast-iron piece, aligns bolts, installs the wax ring, and completes the assembly with the toilet mounted and tested for wobble and leaks.
topics: p ry bar and cold chisel

sections.title: Assess wobble and diagnose flange condition
sections.description: The presenter notes the toilet rocks and has shims, identifies a cast iron closet flange installed at the height of the original floor, and explains that the floor was built up too high, causing wobble. The flange is also described as broken, necessitating removal.

sections.title: Remove old flange and install compression flange
sections.description: The cast-iron flange is broken and must be removed without disturbing the closet bend. The cold chisel is used to break the flange, a flat bar to pry, and floor protection is used. A compression flange with a rubber gasket is then prepared for installation and seating flush to the floor.

sections.title: Mount toilet with wax ring, bolts, caps, and test
sections.description: Bolts are aligned and secured through the new flange into the toilet base. A wax ring creates the seal to the toilet and sewer gases, followed by the nut/washer/base sequence. Brass bolts are trimmed with a mini hacksaw, caps are added, the water connection is tightened, and a wiggle test confirms a tight, wobble-free installation.

featured_techniques.technique: Removal of a broken cast-iron flange with a cold chisel
Prying the flange with a flat bar while protecting the floor
Installing a compression flange with rubber gasket to seal to the closet bend
Centering and aligning closet bolts with the wax ring
Trimming long brass bolts to fit bolt caps using a mini hacksaw
Performing a wiggle test after mounting
